name: Civil Engineering

notes: The Civil file is the BOS-2024 document. Its course table has no course codes, so codes are shown as "code not given".
Several Civil courses are 3-0-2 (4 credits) with theory and lab printed separately in the handbook. Both parts are shown under one course.
The handbook does not list the options for Program Electives 1 to 5, and does not print syllabi for Humanities 1 and 2 or Engineering Economics.

subjects.name: Major / Comprehensive Project
notes: 1. To demonstrate expertise in the chosen project topic, showcasing robust technical knowledge. 2. To apply engineering principles to address real-world challenges faced by industry and society. 3. To develop proficiency in solving intricate problems using a systematic approach. 4. To communicate effectively, both in written and oral formats, with industry stakeholders and the broader community. Details: 6. Students enrolled in the Civil Engineering program are required to select a research topic within the realm of current practices in the field. Collaborative project work is encouraged, with group sizes limited to a maximum of three students. Research areas encompass a wide spectrum including Structural Design and Analysis, Soil and Geotechnical Engineering, Traffic Engineering, Pavement Design and Analysis, Metro and Monorail Construction, Airport Planning and Design, Water Resource Management with GIS and Surveying, Construction Techniques and Management, as well as Environmental Engineering and Energy Conservation. 7. Each group must select a faculty member from the department to serve as their guide. The chosen research topic should align with the interests and expertise of both the group and the guide. Additionally, students undertaking major projects are required to include a one-page section outlining the novelty of their work. 8. Upon completion, the thesis must be formatted according to PDPU standards and submitted to the department through the designated guide. One copy, signed by both the guide and the Head of the Department, will be archived in the departmental library for record-keeping and to verify originality. A review committee consisting of at least two faculty members will assess the internal components of the project and dissertation work, while the external review panel will include an external examiner, the department head, and the guide.
